one_liner: A neural network that, at each step, chooses a handful of features to look at — and lets you read which ones.
plain_explanation: Most neural networks look at every feature at once. TabNet instead works in steps, and at each step it decides which small handful of features to look at — like a person reading a form and covering everything except the two fields that matter right now, then moving on to a different pair. That choosing is done by a learned mask. Because the mask is explicit, you can read it afterwards and see exactly which features the network used at each step — unusual for a neural network, and an interpretability story that does not depend on SHAP.
reference: Arık & Pfister, TabNet: Attentive Interpretable Tabular Learning, AAAI 2021

workflow.label: Normalise input features
workflow.detail: Categoricals → learned embeddings; batch normalisation on the feature vector (numerics also standardised beforehand).

workflow.label: Attentive transformer → mask
workflow.detail: Learn which features to attend to at this step. Sparsemax forces most weights to exactly zero.

workflow.label: Apply prior scale
workflow.detail: Features already used heavily are down-weighted, encouraging different steps to look at different things.

workflow.label: Mask the features
workflow.detail: Element-wise multiply: everything not selected becomes zero.

workflow.label: Feature transformer → split
workflow.detail: Produce a decision contribution and information for the next step's mask.

workflow.label: Repeat for N steps
workflow.detail: Loop to n2. Here N = 4 steps.

workflow.label: Aggregate and predict
workflow.detail: Sum decision contributions, apply the final linear layer.

formulas.name: Attentive transformer mask
formulas.caption: Sparsemax, unlike softmax, drives most entries to exactly zero — so the mask genuinely selects a subset rather than weighting everything slightly.

glossary.means: FC + batch-norm layer of step i
information passed from the previous step

formulas.name: Prior scale
formulas.caption: Tracks how much each feature has been used. With γ = 1, a feature used fully at one step is excluded afterwards. Larger γ (1.3 here) allows reuse.

formulas.name: Masked features
formulas.caption: ⊙ is element-wise multiplication: unselected features become zero for this step.

formulas.name: Feature transformer split
formulas.caption: Output splits in two: d[i] contributes to the prediction, a[i] informs the next mask.

formulas.name: Aggregate output
formulas.caption: Each step adds its (non-negative) decision vector; a final linear layer turns the sum into class scores.

formulas.name: Sparsity regularisation
formulas.caption: The entropy of the masks, added to the loss with weight λ_sparse = 0.001. Pushes masks toward selecting fewer features. (Checked against pytorch-tabnet's source: it computes mean over batch of Σ −M·log(M+ε), divided by n_steps.)

assumptions.evidence: Numerics standardised (fitted on train). Unscaled inputs give badly conditioned gradients.

assumptions.text: Enough data for a neural network
assumptions.evidence: ~28k training rows is small for deep learning; trees usually win here.
cat_idxs / cat_dims passed; each level gets a learned 2-d embedding instead of one-hot.
